items.text: This album is notable for including Strasbourg / St. Denis, a Hargrove composition from its track list.
items.why: Lead: "notable for the inclusion of the composition, Strasbourg / St. Denis"; "All compositions by Roy Hargrove except as indicated". Supported but hollow: it drops why the track is notable ("has since emerged as a modern-day jazz standard").

items.text: 19 to 21 September 2007, at Capitol Studios, Los Angeles
items.why: Infobox "Recorded: September 19–21, 2007"; "Studio: Capitol Studios, Los Angeles".

items.text: Roy Hargrove (trumpet, flugelhorn), Justin Robinson (alto saxophone, flute), Gerald Clayton (piano), Danton Boller (bass), Montez Coleman (drums)
items.why: Personnel matches all five with instruments.

items.text: Before Earfood, Roy Hargrove had made several albums that explored jazz in a hip-hop and R&B setting.
items.why: "following several albums in which he explored jazz within a hip-hop and R&B context".

items.text: This record was a return to his long-running interest in hard bop.
items.why: "a return to Hargrove's enduring interest in hard bop".

items.text: Al Schmitt recorded and mixed the album, with Steve Genewick as engineer.
items.why: "Al Schmitt - recorded & mixed; Steve Genewick - engineer".

items.text: Jacques Muyal is credited as executive producer on the record.

missed: Why Strasbourg / St. Denis matters: it "has since emerged as a modern-day jazz standard". And the pack names tracks to listen for, Di Piero: "listen to 'Joy Is Sorrow Unmasked' and 'Speak Low' ... shut your eyes and you hear the flugel's ancestors", yet listen_for is empty.
